paper_metadata.title: Effect of spark plasma sintering temperature on microstructure and mechanical properties of an ultrafine grained TiAl intermetallic alloy

evidence.quote: the effect of spark plasma sintering (SPS) temperature on the microstructure and mechanical properties of a bulk solid ultrafine grained gamma TiAl alloy produced by SPS of an ultrafine structured Ti/Al composite powder with a nominal composition of Ti–47 at.%Al
the Al, Ti, Al(Ti) and Ti(Al) phases in the as-milled powders were completely reacted during SPS, resulting in formation of TiAl as the major phase, and Ti3Al and Ti2Al as the minor phases.
the coarser grains and better bonded microstructure of the bulk TiAl alloy sample produced using an SPS temperature of 900 ◦C facilitates substantial compression plasticity and work hardening

A Ti/Al composite powder with a nominal composition of Ti–47 at.%Al was produced by high energy mechanical milling (HEMM) of a mixture of Ti powder (99.9% pure, average particle size 150 /H9262m) and Al powder (99.9% pure, average particle size 50 /H9262m) under high purity argon.

The chemical composition of the sintered samples including the oxygen level was determined using Inductive Coupled Plasma (ICP)–Atomic Emission Spectrometry and the inert gas fusion method (for oxygen, carbon and nitrogen contents) to be Ti–31.9 wt.%Al, 0.45 wt.%Fe, 0.06 wt.%Cr, 0.66 wt.%O, 0.48 wt.%C, 0.028 wt.%N.
